about.text: Casein set out of skimmed milk with rennet rather than acid, then washed and dried. It was the raw material of casein plastics such as Galalith and Erinoid, hardened with formaldehyde, and is used today in processed and imitation cheese.

links.name: Gloucestershire Society for Industrial Archaeology Journal (1999), 'The Centenary of Casein'

how.text: Unlike acid casein, rennet casein is not demineralised: the curd keeps its calcium phosphate, so it is insoluble in water and is not made into caseinate directly. It was the raw material for casein plastics such as Galalith.
